category: 2026 DRC-Uganda-France BDBV Outbreak (Active — PHEIC; deadliest and largest ever recorded in DRC)
killed: 2,744 confirmed DRC / 2 confirmed Uganda = 2,746 confirmed total
injured: 2,969 surviving confirmed cases; ~770 currently hospitalized in isolation, 1,269 recovered (DRC); Uganda outbreak closed with 18 recoveries
source: ECDC Ebola Outbreak Tracker / UN News / Forbes — 25–27 August 2026
note: DRC: 5,713 confirmed cases across 58 of 151 health zones in 6 provinces as of 25 August (ECDC tracker, updated 26 August, +57 cases and +29 deaths day-on-day); 2,744 confirmed deaths; crude national CFR nearly 48% per Forbes' 27 August analysis, up from ~20% in early June, reaching approximately 70% in North Kivu province specifically. Africa CDC officials warned 22 August that true case counts could be 2-3x higher (10,000-15,000, Forbes estimates 8,600-10,300) given official detection may capture only 30-40% of infections, and that transmission may have begun as early as February 2026. Uganda: 20 confirmed cases (2 deaths, 18 recoveries) — declared over by its own Ministry of Health 28 July 2026 and confirmed over by WHO on 25 August after completing the 42-day monitoring period. France: 1 case, recovered and discharged 4 July, no secondary transmission. WHO's 100-day review (24 August) found roughly 60% of the ~260 weekly deaths recorded over the prior six weeks occurred in communities away from treatment centers. 155-160 confirmed cases among healthcare workers; Forbes cited 44 deaths (~29% CFR among HCWs). UN Secretary-General António Guterres told the Security Council on 27 August that more than 40 healthcare workers had been killed, roughly 1 million people displaced in Ituri Province, and the response was only 48% funded, appealing for an additional $1.1 billion and warning of 'the virus of indifference.' On 20 August WHO/Africa CDC announced release of 70,000 Ervebo vaccine doses to DRC (20,000 for a Phase 3 Bundibugyo cross-protection trial, 50,000 for frontline/health workers) — the human trial had not yet launched as of 27 August, with a mid-September target.

category: West Africa Epidemic 2014–2016 (Guinea, Liberia, Sierra Leone)

note: 2nd-largest Ebola outbreak in history. CFR 66%. 168 healthcare workers infected, 41 killed. Sustained over 25 months in active conflict zone.

note: Largest single HCW toll: West Africa 2014 (~500 killed). Kivu 2018–2020: 41 killed. 2026 outbreak: 4 killed (as of May 2026). HCW deaths are central to response disruption and community trust breakdowns.

CFR 25% — lowest of any Ebola strain. 149 total cases. Identified new strain BDBV. Index case linked to dead chimpanzee. CFR difference vs EBOV (~60–90%) thought related to different receptor binding.
